ai.title: Add privacy.mdx advanced content page
ai.summary: New web/src/content/advanced/privacy.mdx defines privacy policy. Covers no third-party training, session logging, ad targeting, and backend routing. Future Privacy Mode noted. Internal docs addition.

eli5.text: If you visit Codebuff's help site, you can now read a dedicated Privacy page that spells out how the service handles your conversations and data. The page tells you that Codebuff won't let AI providers train on your chats, keeps session logs only to fix problems, shows ads based just on your current session and basic profile, and routes your requests through its own servers without analyzing your code beyond what's needed to answer you. It also says a stricter Privacy Mode that stores nothing is being built for the future, and you can email hello@codebuff.com with questions. This page is live now whenever you open the advanced-help section.

ai.title: Add Skills documentation
ai.summary: New `skills.mdx` documents reusable instruction sets for Codebuff. Details directory structure under `.agents/` or `.claude/`, `SKILL.md` frontmatter requirements, discovery priority, and `/skill:name` slash command usage. Includes examples for git release and code review workflows.

eli5.text: A new help guide called Skills has been added to the documentation. It teaches you how to create reusable instruction sets that the assistant can load on-demand, such as workflows for git releases or code reviews. You would notice this if you looked at the tips section of the documentation and saw a new page explaining how to organize these instructions in a skills folder, name them properly, and trigger them using the /skill:name command. This guide is live today and provides the rules for how skills are discovered, prioritized, and formatted.

ai.title: CLI default tool renderer collapses unregistered tools
ai.summary: The CLI `ToolBranch` component now defaults to collapsed state for tools lacking a registered custom renderer. Previously, collapse behavior relied solely on `shouldCollapseToolByDefault` or explicit `isCollapsed` flags, causing verbose output for fallback-rendered tools. This change moves the `renderToolComponent` check earlier in the render logic to determine `hasRegisteredComponent`. Scope is limited to `cli/src/components/blocks/tool-branch.tsx`. Tools with registered components retain their existing default collapse logic.

eli5.text: When you run a command, the assistant shows a collapsible box for each tool it uses. From now on, any tool that doesn't have a special custom display will start out collapsed by default, so you see less verbose output unless you expand it. Tools with a custom display keep their old default behavior. Looking at the screen, you'll notice these previously always-expanded boxes now appear folded up until you click to open them.

ai.title: Support .agents/mcp.json for MCP server config
ai.summary: SDK adds `loadMCPConfig` and `loadMCPConfigSync` to parse `mcp.json` in `.agents` directories. CLI `local-agent-registry` merges these servers into base agents, enabling user-defined MCP tools. Env vars in config (e.g., `$NOTION_TOKEN`) resolve at load time; missing vars throw errors. Files: `sdk/src/agents/load-mcp-config.ts`, `cli/src/utils/local-agent-registry.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant can now connect to external tools like Notion or GitHub by reading a simple settings file you place in a hidden.agents folder in your project, instead of needing to configure each tool through complex setup steps. You write your tool names and secret login tokens (like your Notion password) in a plain JSON file, using short placeholders like $NOTION_TOKEN, and the assistant will automatically look up your actual passwords from your computer's secure storage and connect to those tools when you run it. This works today when you build the assistant from the latest code: project-level tool settings override global ones, and if you forget to add a required secret like your API key, it will stop and tell you rather than silently fail.

ai.title: MCP docs move to tips, lead with mcp.json
ai.summary: MCP Servers documentation relocated from web/src/content/agents/mcp-servers.mdx to web/src/content/tips/mcp-servers.mdx. New Quick Start section prioritizes global `mcp.json` configuration in `.agents/` over per-agent TypeScript definitions. Search order defined: project, parent, then global `~/.agents/mcp.json` with override semantics. Examples expanded to cover GitHub, multi-server, HTTP, and SSE configurations.

eli5.text: The instructions for connecting external tools to your AI assistant have moved from a technical guide section to a quick-reference tips section, and now they lead with a simpler setup file that works across all projects instead of a complex code file for each individual assistant. You can now configure tools like Notion, GitHub, or other services using a single easy-to-read settings file placed in your project folder, with the system automatically checking your project folder first, then parent folders, and finally your computer-wide settings file last. This means you no longer need separate setup files for each AI assistant you create, and the documentation includes clearer examples for common services.
